newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close range-trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close range-trading mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed after a moderate-volume session of range-trading.

Marks and Swiss francs, which slowly eroded early in the morning, worked back up toward unchanged and session peaks near midday. But most units carved out increasingly narrow ranges as trading thinned before Thursday's abbreviated futures session and the long U.S. holiday weekend.

June yen futures briefly edged up to the day's peak when a dealer bought some 200 contracts near $0.008158, and brokers also said nearby Canadian dollars caught a late bid but still proved unable to followthrough on the upside.

Sterling climbed to sizable gains, underpinned by expectations that U.K. rates could rise after the U.K. general election May 1, while brokers also noted talk that Canadian rates might head higher after the U.S. rate hike Tuesday.
The Canadian unit had briefly advanced on cross unwinding against the Australian dollar but it subsequently gave up some of those gains.
One floor broker said some players hesitated to buy the Canadian dollar because one large fund reportedly remained short some 7,000 futures contracts.
"People are afraid they know something," he added.
The yen recouped some losses after falling overnight to a new contract low at $0.008128 in June futures, according Chicago Mercantile Exchange data.

Currencies had eased as Treasury bond futures fell after U.S. February durable goods orders overall and ex-defense rose 1.5 percent. Traders had expected February drops of 0.4 percent overall and 0.6 percent without defense orders.

June yen lost $0.000028 to $0.008156, marks eased $0.0001 to $0.5950, Swiss francs dipped $0.0005 to $0.6879, sterling rose $0.0096 to $1.6274, Can dollar rose $0.0029 to $0.7324, Aus dollar up $0.0024 at $0.7839, Mex peso up $0.000225 at $0.122700.
